rules.title: Limit new JavaScript and TypeScript files to 300 lines
rules.text: Keep newly created JavaScript and TypeScript code files at or below 300 physical lines, including comments and blank lines. Split larger implementations into focused modules. Generated files and bundled output are exempt.

rules.title: Avoid expanding oversized existing files
rules.text: Existing files over 300 lines may remain during small fixes, but do not expand their responsibilities; extract new functionality into smaller files.

rules.title: Prefer immutable JavaScript bindings
rules.text: Use `const` for JavaScript bindings that are not reassigned, use `let` only when reassignment is necessary, and do not use `var` in new code.

rules.title: Treat inputs and shared configuration as read-only
rules.text: Do not mutate function inputs or shared configuration; create a copy before making changes.

rules.title: Mark non-mutable TypeScript data as readonly
rules.text: Use `readonly` properties and `ReadonlyArray<T>` for TypeScript data that consumers must not mutate.

rules.title: Keep TypeScript syntax out of JavaScript
rules.text: Do not add TypeScript syntax to JavaScript files.

rules.title: Run behavior checks and tests
rules.text: After changing application behavior, run `npm run check` and `npm test`.

rules.title: Package extension-shipped changes
rules.text: When changing files shipped with the extension, run `npm run package` and include any new runtime modules in `scripts/package.py`.

rules.title: Keep changes focused
rules.text: Preserve unrelated user changes and do not modify existing project rules merely to make a generator test pass.

rules.title: Give modules clear responsibilities
rules.text: Give each module one clear responsibility and avoid placing unrelated helpers in a generic utilities module.

rules.title: Separate major application concerns
rules.text: Keep document discovery, provider requests, suggestion validation, persistence, and UI orchestration in separate modules as those areas grow.

rules.title: Keep the shared prompt model platform-independent
rules.text: Keep VS Code-specific UI and filesystem orchestration out of the shared prompt model so it remains usable in Node.js and webviews without importing VS Code.

rules.title: Inject provider and network dependencies
rules.text: Inject provider and network dependencies so automated tests can simulate success, authentication failures, cancellation, and invalid output without live paid requests.

rules.title: Protect API keys
rules.text: Store API keys only through VS Code SecretStorage; never send them to a webview, include them in project JSON, or print them in logs.

rules.title: Require review before saving generated rules
rules.text: Require explicit review and save before persisting generated suggestions. Cancellation or provider failure must leave saved rules unchanged.

rules.title: Make webview controls accessible
rules.text: Give every interactive control an accessible name and visible keyboard focus, and provide keyboard-accessible alternatives to pointer-only graph interactions.

rules.title: Render untrusted text safely in webviews
rules.text: Escape workspace text and model-generated text before inserting it into HTML; prefer `textContent` when markup is unnecessary.

rules.title: Use VS Code theme colors
rules.text: Use VS Code theme variables for foreground, background, input, and focus colors, with sensible fallbacks.

rules.title: Honor reduced-motion preferences
rules.text: Honor reduced-motion preferences for new animations.

rules.title: Use public-safe demo content for screenshots
rules.text: Capture public screenshots only from this open-source project or another non-sensitive demo workspace; review each image for secrets, personal paths, private repository names, and sensitive conversation text before publishing.

rules.title: Review public assets before packaging
rules.text: Before a release, verify VSIX contents, screenshots, README rendering, icon ownership, branding suitability, and excluded private or development artifacts as separate release gates.

rules.title: Validate installed ConPin separately from package builds
rules.text: Treat package verification and installed-product testing as separate gates: verify activation, Codex compatibility, trust restrictions, repair, restore, and real composer behavior in installed VS Code before publishing.

rules.title: Restore Codex before disabling ConPin
rules.text: Run ConPin: Restore Codex and reload before disabling or uninstalling ConPin; if the extension is already unavailable, use the standalone recovery flow or reinstall Codex.

rules.title: Use canonical docs for generation fixtures
rules.text: When testing project-rule generation in this repository, include AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/architecture.md, and media/AGENTS.md so coverage includes root rules, contribution rules, architecture boundaries, and folder-scoped webview rules.
